userdoc.notice: Per-market, append-only price checkpoints for Siroclimb runs. A run is settled on the checkpoints that were on chain between its entry and its exit, so the result never depends on when settlement is called. Every checkpoint carries the block time at which it was written (not the time the price was observed), which makes "the prices known at time t" deterministic. Three ways to write a checkpoint, each tagged with its source:  - `pushPyth` (anyone, trustless): a signed Pyth Hermes update is posted to the Pyth contract    (Wormhole-verified); every market whose feed is fresh after the update takes its price.    The players' browsers (and the game itself on entry and cash out) do this.  - `pushPublic` (anyone, bounded fallback): for a market without a fresh Pyth price (feed not    covered by the Hermes plan, or Pyth down), public market data is accepted at most every    `PUBLIC_MIN_SPACING` seconds, within `PUBLIC_MAX_MOVE_BPS` of the last checkpoint and within    `PUBLIC_MAX_PYTH_DRIFT_BPS` of the last Pyth checkpoint (if one is recent). Reporters are    semi-trusted within those bounds; the source of every checkpoint is public.  - `pushPrices` (authorised updaters): seeding at deployment and the optional ops keeper. Prices use 10 decimals (sub-cent tokens keep precision, BTC still fits a uint64).
